title: Avatarobots and the crisis of democracy: From bot armies to metaverse swarms
abstract: In this paper, we argue that immersive virtual reality environments, which we call the metaverse, can reproduce and intensify the risks social media platforms raise for democracies.At the center of our analysis are avatarobots, digital agents that resemble human beings, usually in their speech and behaviour, but sometimes also in their appearance, while operating partly or entirely without continuous direct human control.We examine how AI-powered avatarobots can fabricate synthetic majorities, simulate political agency, and distort the signals on which democratic legitimacy depends.To evaluate these risks, we develop the Principle of Accountable Free Expression (PAFE), structured around three criteria: authenticity, non-domination, and verifiability.These correspond to responsibility for speech, insulation from economic domination, and the verifiable origin of political communication.We

title: Tips on writing philosophy papers
abstract: Clarity first; one thesis stated at the start; the philosophical lawyer: argue, anticipate objections and defend against the replies; fewer, deeper objections instead of hit-and-run; no autobiography, over-quoting or sweeping intellectual history.

title: How to write a philosophy paper: A 25-rule guide for undergraduate students
abstract: Twenty-five rules grouped under four standards: writing quality (thesis, roadmap, signposting, relevance, consistent terms), argument reconstruction (premises, the reasons behind them), critical engagement (a modest, original point) and charity (steelmanning, measured language).
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/Cartaya – How to write a philosophy paper. A 25-rule guide for undergraduate students.md

title: Writing a philosophy paper
abstract: A philosophy paper is a reasoned defence of a thesis for an intelligent reader who disagrees: one or two strong arguments developed in depth, objections answered, no fence-sitting, no long introductions or quotations.
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/Horban 1993 – Writing a philosophy paper.md

title: How to write philosophy
abstract: Three principles (a specific thesis, reasons for every claim, objections answered fairly) and a ten-step plan from choosing a topic to formatting; the introduction states the problem, the thesis and the plan of the paper.
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/How to write philosophy.md

title: A guide to writing
abstract: A clear thesis, non-trivial, plausible and non-circular arguments, objections; be forthcoming, organized, brief, specific and plain; examples for every thesis; misused words (infer, refute, true, beg the question); cut needless qualifiers and overstatement.
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/Huemer – A guide to writing.md

aliases: How to write a philosophy paper
title: How to write a philosophy paper
abstract: A guide in three parts: reading philosophical texts (indicator words, charity, mapping the argument), crafting arguments (premises, definitions, deductive and inductive forms, fallacies, total evidence) and grading criteria, with annotated A, B and C sample papers.
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/Jones et al. – How to write a philosophy paper.md

title: A sample philosophy paper (annotated)
abstract: A short paper against an argument of Frege, annotated step by step: plain title and introduction (topic, roadmap, thesis), only the background the argument needs, the opposing argument presented as plausibly as possible with premises made explicit, exactly where the writer disagrees, the writer's argument, the damage assessed, an objection answered, a short conclusion.
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/Mendelovici 2010 – A sample philosophy paper (annotated).md

aliases: Writing your philosophy paper: Common problems to avoid
title: Writing your philosophy paper: Common problems to avoid
abstract: One point, statable in one sentence; the argument as the backbone and the test for what stays; terse introduction with a roadmap; only as much exposition as the argument needs; concrete examples; test every abstract term; a list of words and phrases to avoid.
obsidianPath: Support/Texere/Guides/Writing guide references/Millgram 2024 – Writing your philosophy paper. Common problems to avoid.md

aliases: Guidelines on writing a philosophy paper
title: Guidelines on writing a philosophy paper
abstract: A reasoned defence of a modest claim; outline first; make the structure obvious; be concise but explain fully, for a lazy, stupid and mean reader; simple prose; others presented accurately and charitably; objections anticipated; consistent terms.

abstract: Seven steps (state the question, read, write a thesis, build the argument, outline, write the body first, revise) and ten tips: focus on the question, write for a dull reader, do not overreach, signpost constantly, plain language, support every non-obvious claim.

title: Guidelines on writing a philosophy paper

title: Writing philosophy essays
abstract: Thesis in the opening paragraph; background at most a third of the essay; structures for evaluating, defending and refuting arguments and theses; one argument per paragraph; exposition before evaluation; obscurity is not depth.
